restrictions: Messages m(x) = the 32 little-endian bytes of a 256-bit point x, one padded 136-byte block; f(x) = the complete sha3-256-r6-prefix-v1 digest of m(x) read as a 256-bit value. Two distinct points with equal images give two distinct messages with equal complete 256-bit digests (proof.md Section 2).

Distinguished-point parallel collision search (van Oorschot-Wiener) on f with 256 trails per batch: d = 114 (planes 0..113 zero), cap 9 L, starts R + i from one random word R, a table of 19,000 entries of 32 bytes, one recovery with the selected-round permutation, B = 1361665816212535654038673833664431347 batches (proof.md Section 5).

Each batch evaluates f on 256 trails with a generated bit-sliced straight line of 34,587 register operations (25,074 XOR, 4,953 AND, 3,303 OR, 1,257 NOT; rotations renamed, constants and NOT folded into plane polarities, theta evaluated lazily per chi row, per-row complement subsets), checked against the plain six-round implementation and run by the organizer experiments (proof.md Section 3).

Classical 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5, unit 1626: N = 47776754250108289885528736753876813425013 word operations including recovery permutation calls at 1626 each, every handler bounded; time_log2 = 124.46633 is log2(N/1626) rounded up, by the integer certificate of proof.md Section 6.3.

Machine convention H_reg: a declared file of 2,304 registers of 256 bits, its 73,728 bytes counted as memory; the main loop has no loads or stores. Priced alternatives: 1,024 registers +0.4567 bit, 256 registers +0.8259 bit (proof.md Section 10).

Memory at most 1,035,143 bytes <= 2^20 (straight line 5 bytes per instruction, other code 40 bytes per instruction, registers, lane state, scratch, table), so the memory term of the score is 0 (proof.md Section 4.3). Preprocessing is the generation of the straight line, charged 2^32 operations. No advice.

Success at least 0.3905 for one attempt over the fresh word R, under the score-critical premise H_rand that f behaves as a random function on the evaluated points; the bound subtracts unfinished and cut trails, table overflow, key false matches, Robin Hood starts and the stage-1 halt (proof.md Section 7). No full-scale run and no collision are claimed.

heuristics.statement: Over the algorithm's fresh coins (the random word R that fixes the starts R + i), the images under f of the points the search evaluates behave as those of a uniformly random function from 256-bit values to 256-bit values: conditioned on the history of the attempt, the image of a point not evaluated before is uniform and independent of the earlier images. With it, the probability that the at least M = Q - 480 L points of finished trails contain no two distinct points with equal images is at most exp(-M(M-1)/2^257) = 0.6094986 (proof.md Section 7.4), and the success probability is at least 0.3905.
heuristics.scope: The six-round chain f(x) = H(m(x)) on the points of one attempt: about 2^128.03 evaluations along trails of mean length 2^114 from starts R + i, i < 2^15. Only the pair-collision rate among evaluated images and the distinguished-point rate (density 2^-114 on fixed low bits) enter the bound; trail lengths enter through the geometric law of the distance to a distinguished point.
heuristics.extrapolation: Organizer-executed evidence on the target with the shipped straight line: rho-w22 runs the claimed search end to end at width 22 (expected about 136.9 of 256 successes if the 22-bit chain behaves as a random function, from an ideal-function control of 4,000 attempts at the same parameters); proj-w256 runs eight chained full-width steps from random planes and tests 22-bit image agreements among 2,048 iterates (expected 100.7 of 256). The organizer recomputes every returned pair. Extrapolated from 22-bit projections and 3,584 evaluations per trial to the full 256-bit images and 2^128 evaluations.
heuristics.limitations: A premise about one fixed function; no proof is known and it cannot be tested at width 256. The experiments reach 22-bit projections and chains of at most a few thousand points per trial; the full functional graph, trails of length 2^114 and the 256-bit collision rate are not measured. The bound tolerates a pair-collision deficit eps up to 0.0016; a larger deficit costs 0.5 log2(1/(1-eps)) bits (proof.md Section 8).

heuristics.statement: Machine convention: the 256-bit word RAM of collision-frontier-v5 with a declared file of 2,304 registers; operations on register operands cost one word operation each and need no load or store, and the 73,728 bytes of the file are counted in memory. The cost model fixes no register count.
heuristics.scope: The main-loop straight line (34,587 operations per batch, inputs and digests in registers 0 to 255, temporaries in 256 to 2,303, peak exactly 2,304). Handlers, the recovery and the setup count their loads and stores.
heuristics.extrapolation: None statistical: it is a declared convention. Its price is computed with the same straight line and Belady allocation: 1,024 registers add 12,893 loads and stores per batch (+0.4567 bit), 256 registers 26,750 (+0.8259 bit), proof.md Section 10.
heuristics.limitations: If a reviewer requires a smaller register file the score rises by the priced amount (124.92303 with 1,024 registers, 125.29223 with 256); the success argument is unaffected.
